requirement: Describe the trial as a multinational Phase 2/3 pediatric study with a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, two-period crossover Part 1 followed by a 21-day open-label single-arm dasiglucagon Part 2.

evidence.text: The trial comprises a randomized double-blind placebo-controlled two-period crossover Part 1 and an open-label single-arm Part 2 of 21 days.

notes: Do not describe the whole trial as parallel-group; only Part 1 is randomized and controlled.

requirement: State that 12 patients are randomized 1:1 to placebo then dasiglucagon or dasiglucagon then placebo, with 48 hours per period and no washout.

evidence.text: Patients are randomized 1:1 to the two treatment sequences; each Part 1 period lasts 48 hours and there is no washout.

notes: The absence of washout is intentional and justified by the short half-life and use of the final 12 hours for the primary endpoint.

requirement: Report a planned sample of 12 randomized patients, giving 89% power for a true within-patient mean difference of 7.5 mg/kg/min with SD of differences 7.36 using a one-sample t-test.

evidence.text: With 12 patients, assumed true mean difference 7.5 mg/kg/min and SD 7.36, power is 89% using a one-sample t-test.

notes: These are planning assumptions; the primary analysis uses a mixed model.

requirement: Define the primary endpoint as mean IV glucose infusion rate in mg/kg/min during the last 12 hours of each 48-hour Part 1 treatment period.

evidence.text: Primary endpoint: mean IV GIR in the last 12 hours of each treatment period during Part 1.

notes: Lower IV glucose requirement favors dasiglucagon.

requirement: Derive the endpoint as a time-weighted mean across the final 12 hours, equivalent to IV GIR AUC divided by the observed duration, after converting all infusion concentrations to mg/kg/min.

evidence.text: The endpoint is a weighted mean using actual time periods, corresponding to AUC divided by the length of the period, standardized to mg/kg/min.

notes: A simple unweighted arithmetic mean is not protocol-faithful when observation intervals differ.

requirement: State the primary estimand as the within-patient difference in weighted mean IV GIR between placebo and dasiglucagon in randomized infants with CHI, using observed GIR regardless of treatment adherence or subsequent therapy.
acceptable_values: regardless of adherence or subsequent therapy

evidence.text: The treatment-policy estimand uses actual GIR irrespective of adherence or subsequent therapy and estimates placebo versus dasiglucagon.

notes: The contrast direction should make a reduction under dasiglucagon positive when expressed as placebo minus dasiglucagon.

requirement: Analyze the primary endpoint with a mixed-model regression containing treatment and period as fixed effects and patient as a random effect, and report the treatment difference with a two-sided 95% confidence interval.

evidence.text: The mixed model has treatment and period as fixed effects and patient as a random effect; a two-sided 95% CI is calculated.

notes: Kenward-Roger degrees of freedom are reference-SAP-only and must not be asserted as protocol fact.

requirement: Use two-sided statistical testing at alpha 0.05 unless an analysis is explicitly identified as descriptive or otherwise exempt.

evidence.text: Unless otherwise indicated, testing is 2 sided with significance level alpha=0.05.

notes: The confidence-interval convention must agree with this alpha statement.

requirement: Ask the statistician to confirm the exact primary decision rule and superiority direction because the protocol specifies the contrast, model, alpha, and confidence interval but does not state a complete inequality-based success criterion.
acceptable_values: specific confirmation question for the null/alternative, contrast sign, and CI or p-value threshold

evidence.text: The protocol gives an equality-form hypothesis, placebo-versus-dasiglucagon contrast, model, and 95% CI without a complete operational success inequality.

notes: Do not invent a clinically relevant margin or convert the study to non-inferiority.

requirement: Define FAS as all Safety Set patients with a valid baseline efficacy assessment, analyzed by randomized treatment in Part 1.

evidence.text: FAS includes Safety Set patients with valid baseline efficacy assessment and is analyzed according to randomized treatment in Part 1.

notes: This is narrower than all randomized patients.

requirement: Define PP as FAS patients without major protocol deviations who received both treatments and have primary-endpoint efficacy data for both periods.
acceptable_values: primary endpoint available for both treatments

evidence.text: PP excludes major deviations and patients without both treatments or primary-endpoint data for both treatments.

notes: The final deviation classification is determined before database lock.

requirement: Define the Safety Set as all patients administered any randomized treatment and analyze safety according to treatment actually received within period and trial part.

evidence.text: Safety Set includes all patients administered randomized treatment; safety is summarized by treatment received within period and part.

notes: Part 1 crossover safety summaries must not be bound to FAS.

requirement: Bind primary and key-secondary efficacy analyses to FAS, supportive primary analyses to PP, and all safety analyses to the Safety Set.

evidence.text: Primary and key secondary analyses use FAS, supportive analyses use PP, and safety analyses use the Safety Set.

notes: Population use should remain consistent across sections and tables.

requirement: For a missing primary endpoint, impute the placebo-period value with baseline weighted mean IV GIR and the dasiglucagon-period value with that patient's placebo weighted mean IV GIR.
acceptable_values: missing dasiglucagon uses same-patient placebo GIR

evidence.text: Missing placebo is imputed from baseline; missing dasiglucagon is imputed from the patient's placebo weighted mean IV GIR.

notes: This asymmetric rule is protocol-specified and should not be replaced silently by complete cases or multiple imputation.

requirement: Include the three protocol sensitivity analyses: complete cases; baseline imputation for missing values in either period; and same-patient placebo imputation for missing dasiglucagon with period-specific placebo-group mean for missing placebo.
acceptable_values: period-specific placebo mean for missing placebo

evidence.text: The protocol lists complete-case and two alternative imputation sensitivity analyses.

notes: Tipping-point and placebo multiple-imputation analyses appear only in the later SAP and are not protocol-only requirements.

requirement: Define the key secondary endpoint as total grams of carbohydrates administered by any route per day during each Part 1 period and analyze it with treatment and period fixed effects and patient-level repeated structure.

evidence.text: The key secondary endpoint is total carbohydrates regardless of route per day and uses a mixed-model treatment-period comparison.

notes: Do not narrow this endpoint to gastric carbohydrates only without adjudicating the inconsistent synopsis wording.

requirement: Ask whether and how the key secondary endpoint is gated by the primary endpoint, because the protocol defines both inferential analyses but provides no explicit multiplicity hierarchy or familywise-error rule.
acceptable_values: specific question about gatekeeping, testing order, and alpha allocation

evidence.text: The protocol specifies general alpha 0.05 and inferential analyses for primary and key secondary endpoints but no multiplicity sequence.

notes: Do not infer a fixed-sequence hierarchy merely from the label key secondary.

requirement: Summarize AEs by SOC, preferred term, treatment, severity, and relationship, and summarize vital signs, laboratories, ADA, ECG, echocardiography, physical examination, and local tolerability by treatment where applicable.

evidence.text: The protocol specifies AE incidence dimensions and descriptive summaries of clinical safety measurements.

notes: All safety summaries use the Safety Set.

requirement: Define treatment-emergent AEs as events beginning after the first dose of trial drug and summarize them by treatment received within treatment period and trial part.

evidence.text: AEs beginning after first dose are treatment emergent; safety results are summarized by treatment received within period and part.

notes: The protocol does not state a post-dose risk-window extension beyond observed follow-up.

requirement: Use the IV GIR at the end of the run-in period, the last value before randomization, as primary-endpoint baseline; restart the second period from that run-in GIR.

evidence.text: Primary baseline is the end-of-run-in IV GIR immediately before randomization, and the second period starts from that value.

notes: Do not use a period-specific pre-dose value as the protocol-defined primary baseline.

requirement: State that no interim analysis is planned.

evidence.text: No interim analysis is planned.

notes: Do not add efficacy stopping boundaries.

requirement: Ask for the operational sequence-generation method, block size or concealment mechanism, and randomization-system details before presenting them as fixed SAP facts.
acceptable_values: specific confirmation question covering sequence generation and concealment

evidence.text: The protocol states double-blind 1:1 randomization to two sequences but does not provide the operational sequence-generation algorithm.

notes: Allocation ratio and sequences are explicit; the randomization algorithm is not.
